chunks: It has been narrated from Hudhayfah ibn Mansur that he said:

I was with Abu 'Abdillah عليه السلام in al-Hirah when a messenger of Abu al-'Abbas, the caliph, came to summon him. So he called for a cloak, one of whose sides was black and the other white, and he wore it.
Then he عليه السلام said: 'Indeed, I wear it while I know that it is the clothing of the people of the Fire.'

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu 'Abdillah, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq عليه السلام
key_terms.الْخَلِيفَةِ: the caliph, referring to the ruling authority
key_terms.بِالْحِيرَةِ: in al-Hirah, the location where the event occurred
key_terms.حُذَيْفَةَ بْنِ مَنْصُورٍ: Hudhayfah ibn Mansur, the narrator of the report
key_terms.لِبَاسُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ: the clothing of the people of the Fire, indicating a condemned form of dress

ai.seo_question: Why did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام wear a garment he described as the clothing of the people of the Fire?
ai.summary: This report describes Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام wearing a garment associated with the ruling power when summoned by the caliph. He openly states his awareness of its blameworthy association, indicating a distinction between outward necessity and inner disavowal. The narration also relates to discussions of permissible garments and their moral or symbolic meanings.
